extracted.intended_audience: individual investors in Vanguard mutual funds and ETFs; shareholders interested in proxy voting
extracted.subtask_description: Describes how Vanguard-managed funds approach proxy voting, who casts votes on behalf of funds, and how eligible investors can participate via the Investor Choice program. Focuses on policies, manager roles, and investor information intended to support long-term investment returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of approaches to proxy voting
rubrics_metrics.description: A range of approaches to proxy voting, with a focus on long-term investment returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vanguard offers more than 400 funds managed by over two dozen internal and external investment managers, each with their own policies and approaches to proxy voting. Expect variation by fund and manager rather than a single uniform voting approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxy voting focused on long-term investment returns
rubrics_metrics.description: Proxy voting approaches are pursued with a focus on long-term investment returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting decisions and stated voting policies are intended to be administered in pursuit of each fund’s stated investment objective, which emphasizes long-term returns for investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor Choice participation for eligible investors
rubrics_metrics.description: Investor Choice provides investors in certain Vanguard-advised mutual funds and ETFs the opportunity to participate more directly in the proxy voting process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Investor Choice program enables individual investors in certain equity index funds to express their perspectives on shareholder matters at the companies held in their funds. Participation is limited to eligible funds and investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managers cast proxy votes per stated policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Some two dozen internal and external investment managers cast proxy votes on behalf of the respective funds—or portion of funds—that they manage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers administer proxy voting in accordance with the stated voting policies and in pursuit of each fund’s stated investment objective. This implies that votes are delegated to the manager responsible for the fund and are expected to follow written policy guidance aligned with fund objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency / information for investors
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information and choices for investors about how proxy voting works and how to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page directs investors to learn about what proxy voting is, the ways Vanguard funds approach proxy voting, and how investors can participate in the Investor Choice program—indicating a standard of transparency and investor education around proxy voting practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation and scope of voting authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Proxy voting authority is delegated to the managers who manage the fund or portions of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Votes are cast 'on behalf of the respective funds—or portion of funds—that they manage,' which signals that voting authority may be split among managers for different portions of a fund and that governance of votes aligns with managerial responsibilities.
